headline: Sunny, dry and milder-than-normal weather lasts through Saturday, but a coastal storm is increasingly likely to bring a windy, soaking rain to New York City and the surrounding area Sunday afternoon into Monday morning.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Thursday is clear and mostly sunny in New York City under strong high pressure, with light west to west-northwest winds turning southwest this afternoon at under 10 mph and highs several degrees above normal. Some thin high clouds drift in late, and lows tonight are set mainly by heat escaping under the clear, calm skies. Patchy freezing fog is likely early this morning and again Thursday night in river valleys, sheltered inland spots and the Long Island Pine Barrens; a bit more low-level moisture Thursday night brings a low chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Friday and Saturday stay mostly sunny and dry, with highs in the upper 50s to mid 60s, several degrees above normal; a weak upper-level disturbance passing Thursday night into Friday morning won't bring rain. Nights gradually turn a few degrees milder than normal into the weekend, especially in the city and right along the coast. Fog is increasingly likely on clear nights in outlying areas, particularly river valleys, as the air slowly gets more humid.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A low-pressure system forming off the Southeast coast is expected to move north to near Cape Hatteras Sunday morning and then pass over or near the area late Sunday into Monday morning; the National Hurricane Center gives it a 40% chance of becoming a tropical or subtropical system. If it tracks close, it could bring a windswept, soaking rain Sunday afternoon into Monday morning, with a 30–50% chance of at least 1 inch of rain in 24 hours, a 20–30% chance of 2 inches, under a 10% chance of 3–4 inches, and a low, localized flash flood threat. Winds could reach 20–30 mph with gusts of 35–40 mph if the storm passes over or near the coast, while a track farther southeast or east would limit wind impacts. Drier, seasonable weather is likely later Monday into early next week, with northwest gusts of 20–30 mph possible Monday.

coast: Calm conditions continue on the waters through Sunday morning, with northwest to west winds under 15 knots and ocean seas no higher than 2–3 ft. Small Craft Advisory or possibly gale conditions could develop later Sunday into Monday, depending on the coastal storm's track and strength; the strongest winds (under a 20% chance of 39 mph sustained) are most likely over the ocean waters southeast of Long Island. Minor coastal flooding is possible early next week with the approaching new moon, with a greater threat if the storm tracks over or west of the area.
watch_for: The track and strength of the Sunday–Monday coastal storm, which will decide how much rain, wind and coastal flooding New York City gets.
Whether the low off the Southeast coast becomes tropical or subtropical (40% chance per the National Hurricane Center).
Patchy freezing fog and a low chance of black ice on bridges and overpasses in valleys and sheltered inland areas Thursday night.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in dry, mild weather through Saturday and that a coastal storm will form, but confidence is low on its exact track, strength, rain totals and wind impacts for Sunday into Monday.
